findings.body:
**Handle a tamper refusal of a failed attempt as a per-task refusal, not as a unit-wide infrastructure failure.**

`scanFailedAttempt` throws when `hackDetector` returns findings (`taskLoop.ts:805-810`). The caller sends every throw to the `publishError` branch (`taskLoop.ts:705-714`). That branch sets `indeterminate` and runs `break taskLoop`. The consequences are:

- Every remaining task becomes `'unit stopped for human review'` (`taskLoop.ts:729-737`).
- `!indeterminate` at `taskLoop.ts:742` skips `effects.publish`. Earlier verified commits stay unpublished.

The trigger is realistic. With `pushFailed` on, a failed attempt that adds a default suppression pattern or skips or deletes a test is enough. Attempts often fail for exactly this reason: validateFix's `tamper` gate fails, so `unsafe`/`unsafeRefusal` is already true. `unsafeRefusal` is computed only after the scan (`taskLoop.ts:676-679`), so the scan still runs. Its throw then halts the unit, even though the attempt would never be pushed.

The path-gate refusal at `taskLoop.ts:680-696` shows the intended pattern. It escalates the one task and continues. Tamper findings should take the same path. Infrastructure errors (`tamper.status !== 'ok'`, git failures) can still throw.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

Skip the publication scan when an earlier gate already refused. Return tamper findings as a refusal instead of throwing:

```diff
-            const uploadGate = await scanFailedAttempt(
-              git,
-              bindings,
-              parent,
-              row.failedAttempt.sha,
-              config.protectTests ?? false,
-            );
-            if (bindings.cancelled?.() || currentJobContext()?.signal.aborted)
-              throw new Error('parent job cancelled before failed-attempt publication');
-            const unsafeRefusal = row.validation?.gates.some(
-              (gate) =>
-                ['paths', 'tamper', 'commit'].includes(gate.gate) && gate.verdict !== 'pass',
-            );
+            const unsafeRefusal = unsafe === true;
+            const uploadGate = unsafeRefusal
+              ? ({ kind: 'clean', paths: [], message: null } as const)
+              : await scanFailedAttempt(
+                  git,
+                  bindings,
+                  parent,
+                  row.failedAttempt.sha,
+                  config.protectTests ?? false,
+                );
+            if (bindings.cancelled?.() || currentJobContext()?.signal.aborted)
+              throw new Error('parent job cancelled before failed-attempt publication');
```

```diff
-  if (tamper.value.length > 0) {
-    const finding = tamper.value[0];
-    throw new Error(
-      `failed-attempt tamper gate refused publication${finding === undefined ? '' : ` (${finding.kind} at ${finding.file}:${String(finding.line ?? '?')})`}`,
-    );
-  }
+  if (tamper.value.length > 0) {
+    const finding = tamper.value[0];
+    return {
+      kind: 'protected',
+      paths: finding === undefined ? [] : [finding.file],
+      message: `failed-attempt tamper gate refused publication${finding === undefined ? '' : ` (${finding.kind} at ${finding.file}:${String(finding.line ?? '?')})`}`,
+    };
+  }
```
</details>

A positive denylist result from `bindings.scanPrompt` (`taskLoop.ts:811`) has the same problem. If the scanner can tell "positive hit" apart from "scan failed", route the positive hit to the per-task refusal as well.






Also applies to: 705-714
findings.title: Handle a tamper refusal of a failed attempt as a per-task refusal, not as a unit-wide infrastructure failure.
